plain_description.what: An engineering change: a bounded worker pool with live rate control that lets the version-2 judge send several calls at once. It was checked against all safety guarantees (journal, no double counting, ceilings, preflight) and checked to give byte-identical behaviour when run with one worker.
plain_description.why: Judging is slow when calls go one at a time. Speed must not cost any guarantee about the recorded verdicts.
plain_description.information: Result: done and merged (no live calls). With one worker it is byte-identical to the old path, and no deliberately injected bug went undetected. At the default rate limit the speed-up is at most about 1.17x. It does not show that concurrency leaves live judge verdicts unchanged, or that more workers are safe on a given day. The first live parallel run must declare its settings in advance.
